name: strscan
algorithm: One string kernel per variant over a 64 KiB text from splitmix64 words, reps calls, call r on the text from offset r mod 64: the all-ASCII test, the last 0xFF byte, the UTF-16 length of UTF-8, and WTF-8 validation; the checksum adds each answer and the offset (README.md).

skip.c: no std form of any variant in C: the UCRT has no memrchr, and C has no all-ASCII test, UTF-16 length or WTF-8 validator
skip.mk-wrap: the checksum already uses the wrapping operators; the kernels are std.simd's, whose counters already wrap

no_counts: B24 does not apply: an idiomatic row compares libraries; each kernel's correctness is std/simd/tests_scan.mk's and std/std-simd_vecpaths_test.go's

skip.go: no all-ASCII test of a slice in Go's std
skip.zig: no all-ASCII test of a slice in Zig's std: std.ascii.isAscii takes one byte

skip.rust: no public WTF-8 validator in Rust's std (std::sys_common::wtf8 is private)
skip.go: no WTF-8 validator in Go's std

notes: utf16len: Zig's calcUtf16LeLen, Rust's encode_utf16().count() and Go's range over runes decode every scalar, while Mk's Utf16Len counts bytes (non-continuations plus four-byte leads) and never decodes; the answer is the same on valid UTF-8, the work is not (std10 review N8).
